geometry_edits.rationale: Align the protected public threshold to the verified access side.
Broaden the entry cut to strengthen public legibility.
Deepen the notch vertically for a clearer ground-to-upper void relation.

graph_edits.rationale: Keep the existing dominant bent-bar gesture but strengthen the access-edge response by explicitly aligning the notch/opening to the verified frontage side.
Slightly widen the public cut so the ground threshold reads as a clearer entry seam rather than a minor bite.
Increase vertical reach of the notch to make the void more consequential in section while preserving the main mass.

rationale: The candidate reads as one continuous bent bar with a clear dominant gesture across views, and it remains coherent from isometric, opposite, front, and top. The mass is not a staircase or fragmented stack; instead the bent profile gives a legible directional form with one meaningful public notch/cut near the access edge. The green parcel is respected in orientation and overall containment, though the fit is somewhat generic and could better exploit site-specific openness. The blue frontage is answered by a visible ground seam/entry recess rather than a sealed edge, which is appropriate for neighborhood living. Sectionally, the bent roof/body suggests a calm upper mass and a modest active threshold, aligning reasonably with the program even if the public void is not especially expansive. Overall this is a plausible early-stage neighborhood massing with decent hierarchy and precedent resonance, but it could gain stronger public-space consequence at the access edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference reads more pavilion/cultural than compact street-living; keep its void/bridge logic but not its curvilinear roof emphasis.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise massing with a clearly legible central void and upper bridging can support a neighborhood/public program without becoming generic boxiness.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Sports-mall ring typology is not the same as neighborhood living; do not copy the circular plan.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A perimeter-like mass can still feel public when it frames a sunken or open center and keeps the ground edge porous.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Too large and multi-building for this compact single-mass brief.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like grouping and stepped low-rise coordination can preserve hierarchy while opening a shared court.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Facade/transparency and city-hall civic expression are not the target; borrow only the void-and-overhang relationship.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact rectilinear volume can still achieve publicness through a large carved void and overhanging upper mass at the ground threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference has stronger openness and more site-spread than this candidate; avoid over-flattening into a generic slab.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated horizontal massing with a courtyard void and a calm roof/section can fit a neighborhood mixed-use program well.

warnings: No parcel coordinates were supplied beyond the visible boundary, so containment is judged only from the rendered diagram.
The access response is present but modest; a more legible carved court or notch could strengthen street/public threshold logic.
The silhouette is coherent but somewhat conservative; if iterated, avoid turning it into a generic slab without active ground articulation.
